task_instance: Using the bundled cmux-settings helper, edit a cmux JSONC config file: set app.appearance to dark, enable sidebarAppearance.matchTerminalBackground, rebind the newTab shortcut to the chord [ctrl+b, c], then read the values back, validate the file against the recognized key schema, and confirm hand-tuned non-settings sections are preserved.
tools_used: Bash (python3 running the bundled helper script)
evidence: Skill bundle present next to SKILL.md: scripts/cmux-settings (self-contained Python 3 CLI), references/all-keys.md, references/shortcut-actions.md. Copied the skill into the work dir and created a realistic sample JSONC config (sample-cmux.json) with // comments, a trailing comma, and a hand-tuned non-settings 'commands' section. Ran the helper (python3 ./cmux-settings/scripts/cmux-settings --file ./sample-cmux.json <cmd>). list-supported returned 74 recognized settings paths (loaded from references/all-keys.md), including app.appearance and sidebarAppearance.matchTerminalBackground. set app.appearance dark -> 'set: app.appearance = "dark"'; set sidebarAppearance.matchTerminalBackground true; set shortcuts.bindings.newTab '["ctrl+b","c"]' -> stored as JSON array. get read each value back correctly ("dark", true, ["ctrl+b","c"]). validate -> 'ok: ... parses and all settings keys are recognized' (exit 0). Negative check: set app.bogusKey 123 made validate report 'unknown settings keys: app.bogusKey' (exit 1); unset app.bogusKey restored a clean validate (exit 0). Final dump showed JSONC comments/trailing comma stripped on atomic write while the hand-tuned commands.myCustom section was preserved untouched. All work done in the work directory with --file pointing at the local sample; the default ~/.config path was never written. Note: the real cmux app and its live file-watcher auto-reload are not present in this runtime, but the skill's stated deliverable (view/edit/validate cmux.json by JSON path via the bundled helper) was fully produced and verified against a file.
